blocks.text: Acid rain is rain containing a mixture of nitric acid and sulphuric acid produced by industrial pollution. Normal rain water has a pH of about 5.6 or above, because of dissolved carbonic acid; rain with a pH below 5.6 is acid rain. It is caused by sulphur oxides (SOx) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) in the atmosphere, often from industrial pollution, which react with water and oxygen to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid:

When acid rain falls on soil, H+ ions replace essential nutrient ions such as calcium (Ca2+), magnesium (Mg2+) and potassium (K+) held on soil particles; these are leached out and become unavailable to plants. At the same time it can make toxic metals such as aluminium (Al3+) more soluble; plant roots absorb them and are damaged, which reduces the plant's ability to take up nutrients and leads to slower growth and lower yields:

blocks.long_description: A landscape. Sky: the sun labelled Sunlight with a dotted line to O3; a dark cloud with a box 'Cloud Chemistry: Pollutant Oxidation (SO2, NOx) -> Acid Formation (H2SO4, HNO3) -> Dissolution (Acidic Raindrops)'; rain labelled 'Acid Rain H+, NH4+, NO3-, SO4 2-' and two large drops HNO3 and H2SO4. Right: a factory with smoke labelled 'SOx / NOx Emissions', a house with 'Dry Deposition (SO2 / NOx)', a truck and a car on a road. Ground: 'Natural Ammonia'; a lake with fish, 'Water Acidification (Harmful to Life)'. Left, in a soil section under trees: arrows down, 'Soil Acid Leaching'; H+ arrows to Ca2+ and K+, which are carried away, and to Al3+, 'Aluminum Release (Toxic)'.

blocks.text: Acid rain falling directly on plants can damage and dehydrate the leaves and make the plant vulnerable to disease and environmental stress. It can reduce soybean and wheat yields by reducing nitrogen fixation and nutrient uptake. It can also harm soil microbial communities and disrupt natural nutrient cycles and the decomposition of organic matter.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Why do fish die in acidic lakes? Acid rain releases Al3+ from soil, which clogs fish gills and reduces oxygen absorption, so the fish suffocate.
